answer.rationale: Timeline is the strongest signal available: the release landed ~2h ago and write-path p99 began climbing ~90m ago, so the release is the leading (not proven) suspect, and rollback is the only candidate that removes a suspected cause rather than masking symptoms. memory_b2 explicitly rules out regional_failover here / it cost writes during a hot-write window, which is exactly the current state and directly conflicts with the 'no lost customer writes' objective. add_capacity (memory_b3) worked for a forecast surge with flat queue depth, not for a post-deploy regression, and would likely just absorb symptoms while the defect persists. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) contained an external partner failure; nothing here points to a downstream dependency, and shedding at settlement peak sacrifices exactly the writes we must protect. route_read_replicas (memory_b5) is real relief for primary contention from read load, and it is my fallback if verification undercuts the release hypothesis, but no dashboard/report load spike has been reported. I am spending verification on memory_b1 to confirm the rollback actually completed cleanly with no write loss and that the prior build is genuinely a safe target (a rollback crossing a schema or migration boundary would itself endanger writes), and on memory_b6 because it is the memory that could falsify my plan: if staged gating and canary cohorts reliably surface regressions within an hour, then a regression that escaped canary and only appeared at the 30-minute mark may be load-correlated with settlement peak rather than release-caused, which would redirect me to replica routing or capacity. Downstream risk: committing the single available window to a rollback that is not the true cause leaves us worse off, with the defect still live and no intervention budget left, so I am staging this rather than doing a fleet-wide flip / roll back one guarded cohort of write-path nodes first, hold a short observation window on p99 and write-error rate, and only expand if latency responds. Uncertainty is real: correlation in time is not causation, and I have not confirmed the release touched the write path at all.
